1. (Currently amended) A method for restoring efficiency of a photovoltaic cell that has undergone light-induced degradation, the method comprising: illuminating a photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 5 hours of solar illumination; and annealing the photovoltaic cell at a temperature above 90 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 10 minutes, wherein the annealing is performed after the illuminating step.

2. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell comprises a semiconductor wafer, and further comprising at least one of the following: illuminating the photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 20 hours of solar illumination; illuminating the photovoltaic cell such that the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 16 hours of solar illumination while simultaneously heating the photovoltaic cell to at least 50 degrees Celsius; or irradiating the photovoltaic cell in sunlight using a solar concentrator for at least 10 hours, wherein the solar concentrator increases the irradiance of solar illumination on the photovoltaic cell by a factor of 2 to 5.

3. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is annealed at a temperature above 130 degrees Celsius, and wherein the annealing step further comprises simultaneously illuminating the photovoltaic cell.

4. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 3, wherein the photovoltaic cell receives a time integrated irradiance equivalent to at least 10 minutes of solar illumination during the simultaneous illuminating and annealing steps.

5. (Original) The method of Claim 1, wherein the semiconductor wafer is a silicon semiconductor wafer.

6. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 1, further comprising annealing the photovoltaic cell at a temperature between 140 degrees Celsius and 210 degrees Celsius for a minimum of 2 hours.

7. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is a thin film photovoltaic cell.

8. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 6, wherein the photovoltaic cell is an amorphous silicon thin film photovoltaic cell.

9. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated after manufacturing of the photovoltaic cell is complete, and wherein the photovoltaic cell produces electricity when illuminated.

10. (Currently amended) The method of Claim 1, wherein the photovoltaic cell is illuminated with a light source that simulates light from the sun.
